LEARNING PATH LESSON · SPORTS & MOVEMENT · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Athletics — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches athletics in its three honest words — run, jump, throw — the exact three New Zealand and Australian schools call the heart of movement, and the three every four-year-old is already in love with.

What is this?

Athletics is track and field: sprints and distance running on the track, long jumps and high jumps in the field, throws of every weight — all of it measured, all of it cheered, all of it built from skills children meet in the backyard first.

What does it mean?

Athletics is the mother of sports: nearly every ball game on this wall borrows its run, its jump or its throw. Done on its own, it needs no team, no ball and no rules longer than a breath — the purest gross motor sport there is.

What does the child need to know?

Your child needs three athletics ideas: the sprint begins with a crouch and a WAIT for the word go; the long jump is knees bent, arms swing, TWO feet off together; and the throw turns the whole body side-on and lets the arm arrive last.

Why this matters

Run, jump, throw is the exact phrase NZ’s and Australia’s school curriculums use for fundamental movement skills — teaching the three words explicitly gives a child the keys to every sport that follows.

What it teaches

Sprint acceleration, two-foot take-off with arm swing, side-on throwing with trunk rotation — the three pillars — plus measuring: how far is a really good day?

Words to learn

athleticssprintjumpthrowtrackfieldmeasure

Say this to your child

“"Athletics is three games in one! Crouch down for the sprint — wait for GO, then fly. Bend your knees for the long jump — swing the arms, two feet, FROG! Then turn sideways for the throw — big circle, let it fly, how many footsteps did it go? Run, jump, throw: that is the Olympics of the backyard."”

Step by step

  1. Show the card: "This is athletics — running, jumping and throwing, the Olympic games."
  2. The sprint: crouch low, fingers on the line, freeze… then GO on the word. Practise the waiting — the crouch is half the race.
  3. The long jump: bend the knees, swing the arms BACK then UP, two feet leave together, land like a frog. Measure each jump with a shoe.
  4. The throw: stand side-on, weight back, big arm circle, release pointing at the sky’s window — measure with footsteps.
  5. Run the three-station mini-meet below and close: "crouch, bend, turn — go!"

Look closer at the picture

On this card the word "athletics" is printed big at the top with the game’s scene beneath — the track, the lane lines and the runner exactly as a race day looks.

Ask your child

"What do we do while we wait at the sprint line?" "Do we jump off one foot or two?" "Which way does our body face for a big throw?"

What your child can say or do

Your child might say: "I waited… then ZOOM!" "My frog jump went two shoes!" or the thrower’s report: "It flew six footsteps!"

Out in the real world

Athletics owns every school sports day in the US, Canada, Australia and NZ — and the Olympics bring the whole wall to life every four years. Watch one long jump together and find the three beats: bend, swing, frog.

Try it together

Three-Station Meet: chalk a sprint lane, a jump line and a throw zone. One minute at each — sprint out and back, three frog jumps measured in shoes, one mighty bean-bag throw measured in footsteps. Write the "records" on paper, cheer absurdly, and hand out a drawn medal. That is a real athletics meet, scaled for four legs.

Understanding check

Ask: "What are the three athletics words? What waits at the sprint line? How do we land the long jump?" Run-jump-throw, a crouch, like a frog — three answers and the meet is open.

Parent tips

Measure everything — shoes, footsteps, books. The measuring is what turns running around into ATHLETICS, and comparing your own record to yesterday’s is the healthiest competition there is.

This lesson pairs with the Athletics flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Sports & Movement (Class 37).
